correctness.rationale: For any positive-definite pullback form, averaging over the eight sign/swap isometries preserves its two-sided comparison constants with the norm and yields a scalar Euclidean form; therefore the Euclidean pullback is globally optimal. On the Euclidean unit circle, the fourth power of the norm is exactly \(1+2(\beta-1)s\) with \(s=x^2y^2\in[0,1/4]\), so its extrema occur at axes and diagonals and give the stated two branches. The argument covers every \(\beta\in[0,3]\), including the joining point and endpoints.
